blocks.content:
[]{#necessary label="necessary"}

In order for the linear program $L$ to have any chance of having a solution, the dihedral angles $\Delta$ must satisfy some constraints. Indeed, suppose $L$ has a solution.

::: condition
[]{#dihpos label="dihpos"} All of the dihedral angles must be positive.
:::

blocks.content:
[]{#moduli label="moduli"} In the Introduction we alluded to the cell decomposition of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}$ of Euclidean structures, where the cells are given by Euclidean structures where the Delaunay triangulation has a fixed combinatorial type $T$.
